cards.title: Core idea
cards.body: REST gives each resource its own endpoint and the server fixes the response shape. GraphQL has one endpoint and a typed schema, and the client asks for exactly the fields it needs in one query, cutting round trips, which matters on mobile.

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: REST screens needing related data often make many requests and over- or under-fetch; in the example, 20 images needed 42 requests. GraphQL's cost is server complexity: batching to avoid N+1 database queries, query cost limits, and harder HTTP caching.

questions.q: Does GraphQL solve the N+1 problem?
questions.a: Only on the network. A naive server still runs 1 + N database queries; the server must batch database access.
The client receives more data than it needs.
The client must make extra requests to get missing data.
